verses.text: "Comfort, comfort my people," says your God.
"Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and tell her that her hard service is over, that her sin has been paid for, that she has received from the LORD's hand double for all her sins."
A voice is calling out, "Prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness! Make a straight highway in the desert for our God.
Every valley will be raised up, and every mountain and hill will be made low. The uneven ground will become level, and the rough places will become smooth.
The glory of the LORD will be shown, and all people will see it together. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken."
A voice says, "Call out!" And I asked, "What shall I call out?" "All people are like grass, and all their beauty is like the flowers of the field.
The grass dries up and the flowers fade when the breath of the LORD blows on them. Surely the people are grass.
The grass dries up and the flowers fade, but the word of our God lasts forever."
You who bring good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who bring good news to Jerusalem, shout it out loud! Shout it! Do not be afraid! Say to the towns of Judah, "Here is your God!"
Look, the Lord GOD is coming with power, and he will rule with his strong arm. Look, he brings his reward with him, and his payment comes with him.
He takes care of his flock like a shepherd. He gathers the lambs in his arms and carries them close to his heart. He gently leads the mother sheep that have young.

Who has measured the oceans in the palm of his hand, or measured the sky with the width of his hand? Who has held all the dust of the earth in a basket, or weighed the mountains on scales and the hills in a balance?
Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or taught him as his adviser?
Whom did the LORD ask for advice? Who taught him the right way to judge? Who taught him knowledge or showed him the way of understanding?
Look, the nations are like a drop in a bucket. They are like a speck of dust on the scales. Look, he lifts up the islands as if they were fine dust.
All the trees of Lebanon would not be enough wood for the altar fire, and all its animals would not be enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are like nothing before him. He counts them as less than nothing, as empty and meaningless.
So who can you compare God to? What image can you compare him with?
An idol is cast by a craftsman, and a goldsmith covers it with gold and makes silver chains for it.
A person too poor for such an offering chooses wood that will not rot. They look for a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not fall over.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Have you not been told from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth was founded?
God sits on his throne above the circle of the earth, and its people look like grasshoppers to him. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
He brings rulers down to nothing and makes the judges of this world meaningless.
They have hardly been planted. They have hardly been sown. They have hardly put down roots in the ground, when he blows on them and they dry up, and the wind sweeps them away like straw.
"So who will you compare me to? Who is equal to me?" says the Holy One.

Look up at the sky and see. Who created all these stars? He leads them out like an army, one by one, and calls each one by name. Because of his great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.
Jacob, why do you say, Israel, why do you complain, "The LORD does not see my troubles. My God ignores my rights"?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He never grows weak or tired. No one can measure how deep his understanding is.
He gives strength to the tired and increases the power of the weak.
Even young people grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.
But those who wait for the LORD will find new strength. They will rise up on wings like eagles. They will run and not grow weary. They will walk and not grow tired.
